paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: get ready, because the One who is coming is worth getting ready for. John the Baptist came preaching in the wilderness, "Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is near." (Matthew 3:2) He was the voice calling, "Prepare the way for the Lord." (Matthew 3:3) Repenting means turning toward God, and the baker who turns is the baker who is ready.

Now, John had a warning too, and it's for anybody who thinks being close to the right people is enough. He told the Pharisees and Sadducees, "Produce fruit, then, in keeping with repentance." (Matthew 3:8) He said not to presume on having Abraham as their father, because God can raise up children for Abraham out of stones. (Matthew 3:9) Friend, God isn't looking at the family name on the door. He's looking for a heart that actually turned, and for fruit that shows it.

And the best part is WHO is coming. John said the One after him is more powerful, and that he himself isn't worthy to carry His sandals. (Matthew 3:11) Then Jesus came to the Jordan, and the voice from heaven said, "This is My beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased!" (Matthew 3:17) That's the One we're getting ready for, and it's why my ovens stay warm. So repent, bear fruit, and keep your eyes on Jesus. The story isn't over, friend.
